translationRepairs: You Wudao Rong was from Langye.
s0006 names 由吾道榮: compound surname 由吾 plus given name 道榮, i.e. Youwu Daorong. “You Wudao Rong” mis-segments the name; the proposed English is accurate.
You Wudao Rong was a native of Langye.
Youwu Daorong was a native of Langye.
The same unit’s literal must match 由吾道榮 as Youwu Daorong. The original literal inherits the same false segmentation as the idiomatic line.
He bound his son and offered him as hostage, asking to be beheaded himself if he proved wrong.
He bound his son and offered him as a hostage, asking that the son be beheaded if his prediction proved wrong.
s0030 遽縛其子詣王為質，不勝請斬之: 之 resumes the son just offered as hostage. The idiomatic wrongly makes Wang Chun himself the one to be beheaded; the proposal restores the correct patient.
s0133 names 解法選: surname 解 (Xie) and given name 法選 (Faxuan). “Jiefa Xuan” invents a wrong compound-surname cut; Xie Faxuan is the correct segmentation.
Jiefa Xuan was a native of Henei.
Xie Faxuan was a native of Henei.
The literal field for the same name must likewise render 解法選 as Xie Faxuan, not Jiefa Xuan.
That night Langye’s fifth son urgently summoned Yongluo, claiming an edict.
That night five envoys from the Prince of Langye urgently summoned Yongluo, claiming an edict.
s0167 琅邪王五使切召永洛: 五使 means five envoys, not a fifth son (which would be 第五子/五子). The original idiomatic invents kinship; the proposal matches the Chinese.
That night the fifth son of the Prince of Langye urgently summoned Yongluo, saying it was an edict summons.
That night five envoys of the Prince of Langye urgently summoned Yongluo, saying it was an edict summons.
The literal’s “fifth son of the Prince of Langye” likewise misreads 五使. “Five envoys of the Prince of Langye” is the correct parse and natural English.
